nodes.name: Microfluidic NiFe-LDH synthesis (EG)
nodes.procedure: Initially, 6.73 g of NiC₄H₆O₄·4H₂O and 3.64 g of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O were mixed in 50 mL of ethylene glycol (C₂H₄(OH)₂) under magnetic stirring for 30 min, denoted as solution A. Separately, 1.7 g of Na₂CO₃ and 2.52 g of NaOH were dissolved in 50 mL of distilled water, followed by stirring for 10 min, denoted as solution B. At the same time, the temperature of the microfluidic instrument and the oil bath were raised to 80°C. The flow rate for the Haar alloy pump was set to 60 g⋅min⁻¹, and for the stainless steel pump, it was set to 30 g⋅min⁻¹. Solution A was placed in the Haar alloy pump's raw material bottle, and solution B was placed in the stainless steel pump's raw material bottle. The microfluidic instrument was then started, rapidly yielding the NiFe-LDH_{EG} suspension solution via a T-type tube and a 1 m length pipe. After natural cooling, the product was rinsed with ethanol and distilled water, then vacuum-dried at 60°C.

nodes.name: Conventional hydrothermal NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: First, 3.365 g of NiC₄H₆O₄·4H₂O and 1.82 g of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O were added to 25 mL of water and stirred magnetically for 30 min to form solution A. Separately, 0.85 g of Na₂CO₃ and 1.26 g of NaOH were dissolved in 25 mL of distilled water and stirred for 10 min to form solution B. Solution A was then slowly added to solution B with magnetic stirring. The mixture was transferred to an 80 mL Teflon autoclave and heated at 120°C for 6 h. The product was then rinsed with water and ethanol and vacuum-dried at 60°C.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms (Figure S3) show that the BET surface areas of NiFe-LDH_EG and NiFe-LDH_W were 298.27 m²·g⁻¹ and 285.49 m²·g⁻¹, respectively, both of which are approximately two times higher than that of NiFe-LDH_H (94.31 m²·g⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of NiFe-LDH_EG show diffraction peaks at 11.52°, 23.28°, 34.56°, 39.01°, 60.28°, and 61.25° corresponding to (003), (006), (012), (015), (0015), and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH (JCPDS no. 40-0215), confirming successful formation with high purity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of NiFe-LDH_EG was analyzed through X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns. As illustrated in Figure 2a, the diffraction peaks observed at 11.52, 23.28, 34.56, 39.01, 60.28, and 61.25° correspond closely to the (003), (006), (012), (015), (0015), and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR spectra show broad peak at 3450 cm⁻¹ (O-H stretching), 1635 cm⁻¹ (H₂O bending), 1359 cm⁻¹ (CO₃²⁻ stretching), 1070 cm⁻¹ (O-H translation), and 660-800 cm⁻¹ (M-O, M-OH vibrations).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-IR spectra depicted in Figure 2b reveal a broad peak around 3450 cm⁻¹, in agreement with the stretching vibration of the hydroxyl group ... absorptions in the range of 660 - 800 cm⁻¹ are linked to M-O stretching and M-OH bending vibrations

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra confirm presence of FeOOH at 460 cm⁻¹ and Ni(OH)₂ at 537 cm⁻¹, active phases of the electrocatalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of NiFe-LDH_EG and NiFe-LDH_H (Figure 2c) confirm the presence of FeOOH at 460 cm⁻¹ and Ni(OH)₂ at 537 cm⁻¹ both of which are active phases of the electrocatalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.97 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 873.67 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂) for NiFe-LDH_EG indicating Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺; Fe 2p at 712.67 eV (Fe 2p₃/₂) and 726.05 eV (Fe 2p₁/₂) indicating Fe³⁺; O 1s peaks at 531.14 eV (M-OH), 529.4 eV (M-O), 533.02 eV (H₂O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, the XPS survey spectrum confirms the presence of Fe, Ni, O, and C elements in NiFe-LDH_EG ... the spectrum of the O 1s is deconvolved into three peaks. The peak at 531.14 eV signifies oxygen in hydroxyl (M-OH)

nodes.evidence_snippet: The CV curves (Figure S11) were performed to obtain the double-layer capacitance (C_dl), proportionate to ECSA. Calculated C_dl values for NiFe-LDH_EG, NiFe-LDH_W and NiFe-LDH_H are 0.2515, 0.1981, and 0.1883 mF·cm⁻², respectively
